messages:
Nina: Quick show-and-tell — had to drag my balcony desk inside because of the rain, put the router on a bookshelf temporarily and now my philodendron is flirting with the antenna. Photo: https://images.redwood.example/nina-balcony-2026.jpg. Internet is wobblier than the plant. Anyone tried zip-tying a router to a shelf without murdering the ficus? :seedling:

Rafael: Haha. Short-term: 5GHz if your laptop supports it, and check neighbor channel overlap. Long-term: shelf extender or move the router higher. Also love the plant drama :joy:

Priya: Oof same issue here last month. Quick diagnostic: run a ping to see if it's jitter/packet loss — looks like this when it was bad for me:

Priya: ```
PING 1.1.1.1 (1.1.1.1): 56 data bytes
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=1 ttl=57 time=12.3 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=2 ttl=57 time=118.9 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=3 ttl=57 time=10.9 ms
--- 1.1.1.1 ping statistics ---
3 packets transmitted, 3 packets received, 0.0% packet loss
round-trip min/avg/max = 10.9/47.4/118.9 ms
```

Tooling Bot: network-monitor: observed nina-laptop drop event at 1768463832; 3 disconnects in last 20m, avg RTT 132ms. Suggest switching to 5GHz or enabling QoS for video calls.

Sam: If you can't relocate the unit, cheap powerline adapters worked for me (TP-Link AV600-ish). Or try rotating the antenna perpendicular to the plant — weirdly helps. If all else fails, tether to phone for standups :grin:

Nina: Thanks everyone — ordered a USB 5GHz dongle and a small shelf extender. Will post a "victory" picture if the plant and router learn to coexist. :heart:
